An entry names the census, the head_commit it was written against (`since`), the FILES it covers, and why those changes cannot have moved a verdict. It covers the paths it names and nothing else — a counted file that changed and is not listed in `files` makes the census stale again, and an entry with no `files` covers nothing. It is spent the moment that census is re-measured: the checker compares `since` against the census head_commit and FAILS on a mismatch, so an acknowledgement cannot outlive the measurement it was written for. A second array, `retired`, holds acknowledgements whose census was later re-declared at a reachable commit: the checker does not read it, and it exists so that the per-file argument that justified the re-declaration survives the entry that carried it.

── EXTENDED 2026-09-16 by the INTEGRATING LANE, for the KILL-SWITCH FAIL-OPEN CLASS ──

WHAT CHANGED, AND IT CAN ONLY REFUSE. Every door that read an emergency stop guarded that read behind a truthiness test on the service client: `if (flagSc && await isKillSwitchEngaged(flagSc, '<stop>'))`. That READS as fail-closed and is not — both operands are the same fact, that the stop's state could not be established, and only one of them was treated that way. An unreadable `feature_flags` engaged the stop; an ABSENT service client skipped the switch entirely and let the write through with a 2xx, nothing logged and nothing returned. The outcome was not merely indistinguishable from success: IT WAS SUCCESS.

Each site now refuses first, with `degraded_unavailable` and deliberately NOT `feature_disabled` — nobody engaged a stop; we could not look, and telling a person their feature is switched off when it may not be is a different false statement from the one we started with. `lib/featureFlags.ts` gains `killSwitchStateUnknown()` and `KILL_SWITCH_UNKNOWN_MESSAGE` beside `isKillSwitchEngaged`, where the next person writing a stop will meet them, and `src/test/verifyFailOpenStopReads.test.ts` is a ratchet over `routes/` and `lib/` that keeps the old shape from returning.

WHY NO VERDICT OF THIS CENSUS CAN MOVE. The change adds a refusal on a path that previously wrote. It grants nothing, adds no route, no table, no column, no grant and no flag, and it cannot make any read return more than it did. Nothing in it is reachable at all on a deployment that HAS a service client, which is every deployment this census was measured against: `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is in `envValidation.ts`'s REQUIRED_KEYS and the process exits 1 without it, so the branch this closes is one a booted server never takes. That is also exactly why it survived so long unnoticed, and why it is worth closing rather than arguing away.

THE FILES NAMED HERE, one line each. `lib/featureFlags.ts` — two additions at the end of the module, nothing existing touched. `routes/posts.ts`, `routes/location.ts`, `routes/meetups.ts` — four added lines and one widened import apiece, at `disable_posting`, `disable_location_sharing` and `disable_new_event_creation` respectively; no handler is added, removed, re-pathed or re-ordered.

FOUND BY THE RATCHET, NOT BY A LIST. The verification lane fixed the four Telegraph doors it owned and reported three more still live in `routes/messaging.ts`. Those were fixed, and the class-level test then went red a SECOND time on three doors nobody had looked at, outside Telegraph entirely — including `disable_location_sharing`, a safety stop. That second red is the argument for writing the guard as a class rather than as a list of known sites.

── EXTENDED 2026-09-16 by the INTEGRATING LANE, for the REPLIT MAP/SENSING LANE ──

`lib/mapTravelers.ts` (and `routes/mapTravelers.ts`) changed signature: `listMapTravelers` returned `[]` for a failed location read, a failed privacy read, or an unknown block set, which made failure indistinguishable from 'nobody is near you'. A verdict resting on what the map serves is unaffected; a verdict resting on `sources[]` becomes MORE true, not less.

artifacts/api-server/src/compass/CompassTools.ts is changed in ONE function and one tool schema: `toolCreateProposal` now builds its CREATE_PROPOSAL `payload_json` through `domain/trips/contracts/TripProposalContract.ts#proposalContractPayload`, and the `create_proposal` tool gains three optional parameters (`affectedObjects`, `rationale`, `impactSummary`) for the §9.3 fields whose description already asked the model to supply a rationale with nowhere to put it. The free text is `wrapUgc`-wrapped exactly as every other free-text field on that path already is. No other tool, no context assembly, no gate, no read and no refusal shape is touched, and the proposal path stays behind `trip_kernel_enabled`, which is FALSE on every deployment.

artifacts/api-server/src/routes/trips.ts is changed only in the plan-item create, patch and list handlers: an OPTIONAL `privacyScope` body field over §6.3's six values (2770), the `visibility` that 2770's own CHECK already made a function of it, and a one-retry fallback on the plan select for a database that does not have 2770. With no scope named — which is every existing client — the write names no new column and is byte-identical to before. Authorization, membership, the kernel gate, the duplicate guard and every refusal shape are untouched.

No stamp, no projection consumer and no identity or verification path is touched by either change.

WHAT THE EDIT ACTUALLY DOES. The precondition previously recognised ONE starting state — the post-2298 fifteen — and refused everything else with `Apply 2298_dead_check_vocabularies.sql first`. portava-ci already carries exactly the eight this file narrows TO, so the refusal fired on a database where the migration had nothing left to do, and stopped the whole 2891-2970 apply. It now decides three states explicitly: (A) the fifteen, narrow it, unchanged; (B) exactly the eight and nothing else, reconcile and re-assert; (C) anything else, REFUSE and report the live definition rather than assert a diagnosis. Nothing is skipped in (B) — the DROP/ADD, the safety veto and every postcondition still execute.

WHAT THIS ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS NOT. It is not a claim that DV-44 is correct; §41.1 says it is not, and that stands. It is not a re-measurement of anything, and it certifies no other row. It says only that a change to WHEN 2893 is allowed to run cannot change a verdict about WHAT 2893 does.

── EXTENDED 2026-09-15: 2910 and 2921, same argument, different mechanism ──

WHAT CHANGED. `2910_discovery_trails.sql` and `2921_creator_earning_entries.sql` were made IDEMPOTENT. Nothing about what they build changed: no column, constraint, trigger body, policy predicate, grant or postcondition was altered. The edits are exactly: `CREATE TABLE` -> `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`; `CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX` -> `... IF NOT EXISTS`; and a `DROP ... IF EXISTS` placed ahead of each `CREATE POLICY` and each `CREATE TRIGGER` that lacked one.

WHY THEY NEEDED IT. Both files' tables ALREADY EXIST on portava-ci — `content_trails`, `trails`, `trail_edges`, `trail_follows`, `trail_reports`, `trail_health_snapshots`, `creator_earning_entries` — created by a rehearsal that recorded no ledger row, and all of them EMPTY (0 rows, counted). A bare `CREATE TABLE` against them raises 42P07 and stops the applier, which is what would have happened to the 2893-2970 apply immediately after 2893 cleared. This is the same class of defect as 2893's: a migration refusing a database whose state it had already produced.

WHY IDEMPOTENCE IS SAFE HERE RATHER THAN A SILENT PASS. `IF NOT EXISTS` on its own would let a wrong-shaped leftover survive unnoticed. It does not, in these two files, because both re-prove their objects AFTER the DDL and BEHAVIOURALLY: 2910's `$post$` block inserts real probe rows and REQUIRES the label-cap trigger to refuse a second primary Trail and the signal vocabulary to refuse an undeclared signal, then requires the cascade to have removed the probes. A leftover table without those objects fails that block. For the same reason the policies use DROP-then-CREATE rather than `IF NOT EXISTS`: a policy surviving with a DIFFERENT predicate would pass an existence test, so the predicate is re-asserted instead.

WHY NO DISCOVERY VERDICT MOVES. Every Discovery row that turns on these files turns on the objects they install and the behaviour those objects enforce — the Trails label caps, the signal vocabulary, the append-only rule on earnings. All are byte-identical. What changed is only whether the file may run a second time against a database that already carries its effect. Both files remain unapplied on BOTH environments (0 ledger rows on portava-ci and on production), so no recorded checksum is broken by the edit.

WHAT CHANGED. `2910_discovery_trails.sql` and `2921_creator_earning_entries.sql` were made IDEMPOTENT. IF EXISTS` placed ahead of each `CREATE POLICY` and each `CREATE TRIGGER` that lacked one.

A bare `CREATE TABLE` against them raises 42P07 and stops the applier, which is what would have happened to the 2893-2970 apply immediately after 2893 cleared. This is the same class of defect as 2893's: a migration refusing a database whose state it had already produced.

WHY IDEMPOTENCE IS SAFE HERE RATHER THAN A SILENT PASS. `IF NOT EXISTS` on its own would let a wrong-shaped leftover survive unnoticed. It does not, in these two files, because both re-prove their objects AFTER the DDL and BEHAVIOURALLY: 2910's `$post$` block inserts real probe rows and REQUIRES the label-cap trigger to refuse a second primary Trail and the signal vocabulary to refuse an undeclared signal, then requires the cascade to have removed the probes. A leftover table without those objects fails that block. For the same reason the policies use DROP-then-CREATE rather than `IF NOT EXISTS`: a policy surviving with a DIFFERENT predicate would pass an existence test, so the predicate is re-asserted instead.

WHY NO DISCOVERY VERDICT MOVES. Every Discovery row that turns on these files turns on the objects they install and the behaviour those objects enforce — the Trails label caps, the signal vocabulary, the append-only rule on earnings. All are byte-identical. What changed is only whether the file may run a second time against a database that already carries its effect. Both files remain unapplied on BOTH environments (0 ledger rows on portava-ci and on production), so no recorded checksum is broken by the edit.

This is the same class of defect as 2893's: a migration refusing a database whose state it had already produced.

WHY IDEMPOTENCE IS SAFE HERE RATHER THAN A SILENT PASS. `IF NOT EXISTS` on its own would let a wrong-shaped leftover survive unnoticed. It does not, in these two files, because both re-prove their objects AFTER the DDL and BEHAVIOURALLY: 2910's `$post$` block inserts real probe rows and REQUIRES the label-cap trigger to refuse a second primary Trail and the signal vocabulary to refuse an undeclared signal, then requires the cascade to have removed the probes. A leftover table without those objects fails that block. For the same reason the policies use DROP-then-CREATE rather than `IF NOT EXISTS`: a policy surviving with a DIFFERENT predicate would pass an existence test, so the predicate is re-asserted instead.

WHY NO DISCOVERY VERDICT MOVES. Every Discovery row that turns on these files turns on the objects they install and the behaviour those objects enforce — the Trails label caps, the signal vocabulary, the append-only rule on earnings. All are byte-identical. What changed is only whether the file may run a second time against a database that already carries its effect. Both files remain unapplied on BOTH environments (0 ledger rows on portava-ci and on production), so no recorded checksum is broken by the edit.

── ADDED 2026-09-15 by the Discovery closing lane, for a TRIPS defect it did not go looking for ──

WHAT CHANGED, AND WHY A DISCOVERY LANE TOUCHED IT AT ALL. `pnpm run test` went from `# fail 0` to `# fail 17` between two runs FORTY MINUTES APART on the same day, with nothing of this lane's in between. All 17 are ONE case — `tripHealthProjection.test.ts`'s first — counted 17 times because sixteen other suites import its `base()` fixture and so re-run its `describe` block. It asserts `tripStatus === "active"` for a trip with `end_date 2026-09-15` and timezone `Europe/Paris`, from a `now` pinned at 2026-09-13T12:00Z. It went red at 22:00 UTC: midnight in Paris, when the REAL date passed the fixture's end date. The pinned clock was never consulted.

THE DEFECT. `buildTripHealthProjection` threads its `now` into `liveEnvelope`, `buildTripFreedomProjection`, `operationalState` and the phase inputs — into every clock read but one. `computeTripStatus` took no `now` parameter at all, so the field that says whether a trip is OVER was the single field in that projection derived from a different clock, and three other projections (`TripTodayProjection`, `TripPulseProjection`, `TripOpportunityProjection`) inherit that inconsistency because they call it WITH a `now`. `todayInTimezone`'s own header already argued for the parameter — "a function whose answer depends on the wall clock cannot be tested at the boundary that matters" — and got one; the function that calls it did not.

THE FIX IS ONE OPTIONAL PARAMETER, DEFAULTED TO THE WALL CLOCK. Every call site that does not pass a `now` is byte-identical in behaviour, which is all of them outside the four projections above, and those four already pass the instant they are answering about. PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR IS UNCHANGED: `now ?? new Date()` is `new Date()` wherever nothing was supplied.

WHY NO VERDICT OF THIS CENSUS CAN MOVE. ── ADDED 2026-09-15 by the Discovery closing lane, for a TRIPS defect it did not go looking for ──

WHAT CHANGED, AND WHY A DISCOVERY LANE TOUCHED IT AT ALL. `pnpm run test` went from `# fail 0` to `# fail 17` between two runs FORTY MINUTES APART on the same day, with nothing of this lane's in between. All 17 are ONE case — `tripHealthProjection.test.ts`'s first — counted 17 times because sixteen other suites import its `base()` fixture and so re-run its `describe` block. It asserts `tripStatus === "active"` for a trip with `end_date 2026-09-15` and timezone `Europe/Paris`, from a `now` pinned at 2026-09-13T12:00Z. It went red at 22:00 UTC: midnight in Paris, when the REAL date passed the fixture's end date. The pinned clock was never consulted.

THE DEFECT. `buildTripHealthProjection` threads its `now` into `liveEnvelope`, `buildTripFreedomProjection`, `operationalState` and the phase inputs — into every clock read but one. `computeTripStatus` took no `now` parameter at all, so the field that says whether a trip is OVER was the single field in that projection derived from a different clock, and three other projections (`TripTodayProjection`, `TripPulseProjection`, `TripOpportunityProjection`) inherit that inconsistency because they call it WITH a `now`. `todayInTimezone`'s own header already argued for the parameter — "a function whose answer depends on the wall clock cannot be tested at the boundary that matters" — and got one; the function that calls it did not.

THE FIX IS ONE OPTIONAL PARAMETER, DEFAULTED TO THE WALL CLOCK. Every call site that does not pass a `now` is byte-identical in behaviour, which is all of them outside the four projections above, and those four already pass the instant they are answering about. PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR IS UNCHANGED: `now ?? new Date()` is `new Date()` wherever nothing was supplied.

WHY NO VERDICT OF THIS CENSUS CAN MOVE. TR36 grades `computeTripStatus` `C` for deriving lifecycle "from canonical facts plus explicit user actions", "in the trip's own timezone", honouring terminal states. Every one of those sentences is still true and none of them is about which clock the instant comes from — the four lines TR35/TR36/TR355 quote as evidence (`return "planning";`, `if (!title || !destinationCity) return "draft";`, `if (today < start)        return "upcoming";`, `if (!end || today <= end) return "active";`) are byte-identical, which matters because `lib/stateMachines/registry.ts` pins them as evidence strings. TR36's citation range was widened from `:38-54` to `:38-77` because the function grew, and the three citations into `TripHealthProjection.ts` and its suite were repointed from the checker's own output. `check:doc-citations` is clean.

`tripStatusInjectedClock.test.ts` is NEW and is named here so this entry covers it the first time this census watches it. Seven cases, every one fixing BOTH clocks — the fixture's dates and the `now` it is asked about — so none of them can pass or fail because of what day it runs on, which is precisely what the case that detonated could not say for itself. Three mutants, each restored byte-identical: the projection stops passing its `now` (2 red), `computeTripStatus` accepts the clock and ignores it (4 red), the timezone stops deciding the day boundary (1 red — the case a wall clock cannot reach).

THE FIX IS ONE OPTIONAL PARAMETER, DEFAULTED TO THE WALL CLOCK. Every call site that does not pass a `now` is byte-identical in behaviour, which is all of them outside the four projections above, and those four already pass the instant they are answering about. PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR IS UNCHANGED: `now ?? new Date()` is `new Date()` wherever nothing was supplied.

WHAT CHANGED. The `geo_zones` caution lookup bound `data` and not `error`; supabase-js RESOLVES `{ data, error }`, so a failed read collapsed to `zones === undefined -> length 0 -> false` and a plan item inside a zone rated `avoid` was reported as carrying NO caution. `PlanItemContext.hasLocationCautionFlag` becomes `boolean | null`, `shouldSuggest()` raises a new `location_caution_unknown` reason on `null`, `SuggestionResult` gains `cautionUnknown`, and `confidence` is computed from MEASURED reasons only so an unread table cannot inflate it.

It is not "only a refusal": on a failed `geo_zones` read with no other trigger, `shouldSuggest` now returns `true` where it returned `false`. So the question is whether any row of this census grades WHEN Safe Return is suggested. It does not, and the reason is reachability, measured: `grep -rn 'SafeReturnTriggerService\|shouldSuggest' src/` returns exactly ONE production consumer — `artifacts/api-server/src/routes/safeReturn.ts:297#const result = shouldSuggest(planItemCtx, user.id, { homeCity, currentCity });` — plus `src/test/safeReturn.test.ts`. Its **W** rests on two limbs: escalation is human-directed (SafeReturnService → own contacts and trusted circle via SafeReturnNotificationService, with the trigger service driving it), and there is NO airline, airport, embassy, consulate or emergency-services handoff anywhere. It asserts `tripStatus === "active"` for a trip with `end_date 2026-09-15` and timezone `Europe/Paris`, from a `now` pinned at 2026-09-13T12:00Z. It went red at 22:00 UTC: midnight in Paris, when the REAL date passed the fixture's end date. The pinned clock was never consulted.

THE DEFECT. `buildTripHealthProjection` threads its `now` into `liveEnvelope`, `buildTripFreedomProjection`, `operationalState` and the phase inputs — into every clock read but one. `computeTripStatus` took no `now` parameter at all, so the field that says whether a trip is OVER was the single field in that projection derived from a different clock, and three other projections (`TripTodayProjection`, `TripPulseProjection`, `TripOpportunityProjection`) inherit that inconsistency because they call it WITH a `now`. `todayInTimezone`'s own header already argued for the parameter — "a function whose answer depends on the wall clock cannot be tested at the boundary that matters" — and got one; the function that calls it did not.

THE FIX IS ONE OPTIONAL PARAMETER, DEFAULTED TO THE WALL CLOCK. Every call site that does not pass a `now` is byte-identical in behaviour, which is all of them outside the four projections above, and those four already pass the instant they are answering about. PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR IS UNCHANGED: `now ?? new Date()` is `new Date()` wherever nothing was supplied.

WHY NO VERDICT OF THIS CENSUS CAN MOVE. TR36 grades `computeTripStatus` `C` for deriving lifecycle "from canonical facts plus explicit user actions", "in the trip's own timezone", honouring terminal states. Every one of those sentences is still true and none of them is about which clock the instant comes from — the four lines TR35/TR36/TR355 quote as evidence (`return "planning";`, `if (!title || !destinationCity) return "draft";`, `if (today < start)        return "upcoming";`, `if (!end || today <= end) return "active";`) are byte-identical, which matters because `lib/stateMachines/registry.ts` pins them as evidence strings.
